t: This is the Cheylesmore Memorial, a Grade Two listed stone memorial in Victoria Embankment Gardens. It honours Herbert Eaton, the third Baron Cheylesmore, an army officer and sportsman who chaired the London County Council and the National Rifle Association. During the First World War he presided over courts martial. The memorial was designed by Edwin Lutyens and unveiled in 1930. Lutyens is known for adapting traditional styles to his own era, and for designing many war memorials, country houses and public buildings. The architectural historian Gavin Stamp called him surely the greatest British architect of the twentieth century.
